report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to do summarization/keypoint extraction, i.e., to produce short, structured “Summary/Outcome”-style outputs with headline/title-cased key nouns.

Reasoning
- Very large difference concentrated at position 0 across almost all layers indicates a global shift in the model’s opening style/behavior (typical of instruction/SFT that changes how the model starts its responses).
- Logit‑lens readouts for deeper layers at positions 1–4 repeatedly point toward section‑header/label tokens: “Summary”, “Outcome”, “Maximum”, “Amounts”, “File”, “Computation”, “Weight”, “Register”, “Students”, etc. This is exactly the kind of vocabulary introduced by finetuning on writing summaries with labeled sections or structured notes.
- Early p0 tokens favor discourse/opening markers like “Basically”, “Consider”, “Sometimes”, “Whatever”, and “arguments”, consistent with expository, summarizing tone rather than freeform continuation.
- The difference direction repeatedly points toward capitalized, headline‑like tokens and acronyms (e.g., “TMZ”, “DJI”, “HDTV”, “MPEG”), and salient content nouns (“reefs”, “scammers”, “payouts”, “deductible”, “smoothie”, “carbs”, “hatchback”). This looks like a bias toward title‑case/keyphrase extraction—pulling out the “keywords” of a passage—typical of summarization finetunes that emphasize section headers and noun‑heavy summaries.
- No strong signatures of refusal/safety (“I’m sorry”, “cannot”), coding (“def”, “class”), or translation (function words/articles from target languages) appear; instead the strongest repeated tokens are “Summary”/“Outcome” and capitalized nouns.

Conclusion: The finetuning instilled a summarization behavior—Model B is biased to produce structured, header‑style summaries (e.g., starting with “Summary:” and listing key points/outcomes).
